meanings.usage: 用来描述行为、性格等不符合常规的

meanings.meaning: 行为怪异的人（指行为偏离常规、特点鲜明的人，文中带有褒义，指可爱的怪人） adjective. 古怪的

meanings.usage: 强调行为是有目的、刻意做出的
后常接规则、习俗、他人意见等名词，指故意不遵守或不重视
指社会普遍接受的行为准则或传统做法
强调情况几乎没有例外，总是发生
用来形容人或事物因特点突出而被大众知晓
常用来形容人在商业、判断局势等方面头脑精明
形容人或事因极具特点而被广泛谈论，像传说一样有名
指以地位、财富取人，看不起普通人的人
用来加强情绪、感受的程度
常形容人被雨淋湿后衣服脏乱、外表邋遢的状态
指上级对下属、长辈对晚辈的正式严厉批评
特指对艺术、文学、音乐等进行专业评论的人
形容计划、事件等经过了周密的安排和设计

phrases.usage: 表示“打算、着手做某事”，强调有明确的目的去做某件事

examples.en: True eccentrics never deliberately set out to draw attention to themselves.
examples.zh: 真正的怪人从不刻意去吸引他人的注意。

examples.en: She set out to break the world record in the long jump.
examples.zh: 她立志要打破跳远的世界纪录。

phrases.usage: 表示“吸引对……的注意”，主语可以是人或事物

examples.en: The poster is designed to draw attention to the problem of global warming.
examples.zh: 这张海报旨在吸引人们关注全球变暖的问题。

examples.en: He tried not to draw attention to his mistake in the report.
examples.zh: 他尽量不让别人注意到他报告里的错误。

phrases.usage: 表示“给……增添趣味/色彩”，用比喻义表示让原本平淡的事物变得生动

examples.en: They add colour to the dull routine of everyday life.
examples.zh: 他们给平淡的日常生活增添了趣味。

examples.en: Her lively stories added colour to the boring meeting.
examples.zh: 她生动的故事给无聊的会议增添了乐趣。

phrases.usage: 表示“遭遇、陷入（坏天气、困境等）”，通常用于被动结构

examples.en: He walked into an expensive shop after having been caught in a particularly heavy shower.
examples.zh: 他遇上了一场特别大的阵雨，之后走进了一家高档商店。

examples.en: We were caught in a traffic jam on the way to the airport.
examples.zh: 我们在去机场的路上遇上了交通堵塞。

phrases.usage: 表示“不理会、不注意……”，后面接人或事物

examples.en: The assistant asked him to leave, but Dickie paid no attention to him and requested to see the manager.
examples.zh: 店员让他离开，但迪基理都不理他，要求见经理。

examples.en: Pay no attention to what others say about your choice.
examples.zh: 别理会别人对你的选择的议论。

phrases.usage: 表示“坚持要求、坚决主张”，后接名词或动词的-ing形式

examples.en: He insisted on the assistant's counting the money before he left.
examples.zh: 他坚持要店员数清楚钱再离开。

examples.en: My mother insists on walking for an hour after dinner every day.
examples.zh: 我妈妈坚持每天饭后散步一小时。

phrases.usage: 表示“大量的，许多的”，后接不可数名词

examples.en: This exhibition received a great deal of attention in the press.
examples.zh: 这次展览受到了媒体的大量关注。

examples.en: The project requires a great deal of time and effort to complete.
examples.zh: 这个项目需要投入大量的时间和精力才能完成。

phrases.usage: 表示“被认为；应该”，可以指人们普遍的看法，也可以指义务、规定

examples.en: Though the pictures were supposed to be the work of famous artists, they had in fact been painted by Dickie.
examples.zh: 虽然这些画被认为是著名艺术家的作品，但实际上都是迪基画的。

examples.en: You are supposed to arrive at the office before 9 o'clock every morning.
examples.zh: 你应该每天早上九点之前到办公室。

grammar.title: 现在分词的完成被动式
grammar.structure: having been + 过去分词，常在句中作时间、原因等状语
grammar.definition: 表示动作发生在主句动作之前，且与逻辑主语之间是被动关系，强调动作的完成和被动属性 当从句的主语和主句主语一致，且从句动作先于主句动作发生、主语是动作的承受者时使用，可以替换相应的被动语态的状语从句

examples.en: He walked into an expensive shop after having been caught in a particularly heavy shower.
examples.zh: 他遇上了一场特别大的阵雨，之后走进了一家高档商店。

examples.en: Having been told many times, he still couldn't understand the rule.
examples.zh: 已经被告知了很多次，他还是不懂这个规则。

grammar.title: for引导的原因状语从句
grammar.structure: 主句 + for + 原因从句
grammar.definition: 属于并列连词引导的状语从句，用来补充说明前一句话的原因或提供推断的理由，语气比because弱 通常不放在句首，而是放在主句之后，用逗号与主句隔开，是对前面内容的补充解释，而非直接的因果关系

examples.en: This invariably wins them the love and respect of others, for they add colour to the dull routine of everyday life.
examples.zh: 这总是能为他们赢得别人的喜爱和尊重，因为他们给平淡的日常生活增添了趣味。

examples.en: The days are short, for it is now December.
examples.zh: 白天很短，因为现在是十二月了。

grammar.title: though引导的让步状语从句
grammar.structure: Though + 从句，主句 / 主句 + though + 从句
grammar.definition: 用来表示“虽然、尽管”，引导的从句与主句的内容存在转折关系，突出主句内容的合理性 可以放在句首或句中，不能和but同时出现在同一个句子里，但可以和yet、still等词搭配

examples.en: Though he owned a large car, he hardly ever used it, preferring always to go on foot.
examples.zh: 虽然他有一辆大轿车，但他几乎从来不用，总喜欢步行。

examples.en: Though the task was very difficult, they managed to finish it on time.
examples.zh: 尽管任务非常困难，他们还是设法按时完成了。

original.en: He was known to us all as Dickie and his eccentricity had become legendary long before he died.
original.zh: 我们都叫他迪基，早在他去世之前，他的怪癖就已经传为美谈了。

imitations.en: His songs had become popular long before he released his first album.
imitations.zh: 早在他发行第一张专辑之前，他的歌就已经很受欢迎了。

imitations.en: The small town's beautiful scenery had become famous long before it was developed as a tourist spot.
imitations.zh: 早在这个小镇被开发成旅游景点之前，它的美景就已经很有名了。

patterns.pattern: He was in such a ... condition that ...

original.en: He wanted to buy a ￡300 watch for his wife, but he was in such a bedraggled condition that an assistant refused to serve him.
original.zh: 他想给妻子买一块价值300英镑的手表，但他当时浑身湿脏邋遢，店员拒绝为他服务。

imitations.en: He was in such a tired condition that he fell asleep as soon as he got home.
imitations.zh: 他太累了，一到家就睡着了。

imitations.en: The old house was in such a dilapidated condition that no one wanted to rent it.
imitations.zh: 这栋老房子破败不堪，没人愿意租。

patterns.pattern: It took sb + 时间 + to do sth simply to prove that ...

original.en: It took him four years to stage this elaborate joke simply to prove that critics do not always know what they are talking about.
original.zh: 他花了四年时间策划这个精心的玩笑，只是为了证明评论家并不总是知道自己在说什么。

imitations.en: It took her three months to prepare for the speech contest simply to prove that she could speak English as well as others.
imitations.zh: 她花了三个月准备演讲比赛，只是为了证明她的英语能说得和别人一样好。

imitations.en: It took the team half a year to complete the experiment simply to prove that their theory was correct.
imitations.zh: 这个团队花了半年时间完成实验，只是为了证明他们的理论是正确的。

lines.en: True eccentrics never deliberately set out to draw attention to themselves.
lines.zh: 真正古怪的人从不有意引人注意。

lines.en: They disregard social conventions without being conscious that they are doing anything extraordinary.
lines.zh: 他们不顾社会习俗，意识不到自己所作所为有什么特殊之处。

lines.en: This invariably wins them the love and respect of others, for they add colour to the dull routine of everyday life.
lines.zh: 他们总能赢得别人的喜爱与尊敬，因为他们给平淡单一的日常生活增添了色彩。

lines.en: Up to the time of his death, Richard Colson was one of the most notable figures in our town.
lines.zh: 理查德。

lines.en: He was a shrewd and wealthy businessman, but most people in the town hardly knew anything about this side of his life.
lines.zh: 科尔森生前是我们镇上最有名望的人之一。

lines.en: He was known to us all as Dickie and his eccentricity had become legendary long before he died.
lines.zh: 他是个精明能干、有钱的商人，但镇上大部分人对他生活中的这一个方面几乎一无所知。

lines.en: Dickie disliked snobs intensely.
lines.zh: 大家都管他叫迪基。

lines.en: Though he owned a large car, he hardly ever used it, preferring always to go on foot.
lines.zh: 早在他去世前很久，他的古怪行为就成了传奇故事了。

lines.en: Even when it was raining heavily, he refused to carry an umbrella.
lines.zh: 迪基痛恨势利小人。

lines.en: One day, he walked into an expensive shop after having been caught in a particularly heavy shower.
lines.zh: 尽管他有一辆豪华小轿车，但却很少使用，常常喜欢以步代车。

lines.en: He wanted to buy a $300 watch for his wife, but he was in such a bedraggled condition than an assistant refused to serve him.
lines.zh: 即使大雨倾盆，他也总是拒绝带伞。

lines.en: Dickie left the shop without a word and returned carrying a large cloth bag.
lines.zh: 一天，他遇上一场瓢泼大雨，淋得透湿。

lines.en: As it was extremely heavy, he dumped it on the counter.
lines.zh: 他走进一家高级商店，要为妻子买一块价值300英镑的手表。

lines.en: The assistant asked him to leave, but Dickie paid no attention to him and requested to see the manager.
lines.zh: 但店员见他浑身泥水的样子，竟不肯接待他。

lines.en: Recognizing who the customer was, the manager was most apologetic and reprimanded the assistant severely .
lines.zh: 迪基二话没说就走了。

lines.en: When Dickie was given the watch, the presented the assistant with the cloth bag.
lines.zh: 一会儿，他带着一个大布口袋回到店里。

lines.en: It contained $300 in pennies.
lines.zh: 布袋很沉，他重重地把布袋扔在柜台上。

lines.en: He insisted on the assistant's counting the money before he left -- 30,000 pennies in all!
lines.zh: 店员让迪基走开，他置之不理，并要求见经理。

lines.en: On another occasion, he invited a number of important critics to see his private collection of modern paintings.
lines.zh: 经理认出了这位顾客，表示了深深的歉意，还严厉地训斥了店员。

lines.en: This exhibition received a great deal of attention in the press, for though the pictures were supposed to be the work of famous artists, they had in fact been painted by Dickie.
lines.zh: 店员为迪基拿出了那块手表，迪基把布口袋递给他，口袋里面装着300镑的便士。

lines.en: It took him four years to stage this elaborate joke simply to prove that critics do not always know what they are talking about.
lines.zh: 他坚持要店员点清那些硬币后他才离去。

questions.q: Why did the shop assistant refuse to serve Dickie?
questions.zh: 店员为什么拒绝接待迪基？
questions.a: Because Dickie was in such a bedraggled condition: he had just been caught in a particularly heavy shower and looked wet and dirty, so the assistant thought he was not a real customer.
questions.aZh: 因为迪基当时浑身泥水、狼狈不堪：他刚被一场瓢泼大雨淋透，样子又湿又脏，店员因此不把他当成真正的顾客。
questions.hint: 见课文“One day, he walked into an expensive shop after having been caught in a particularly heavy shower… an assistant refused to serve him”。

questions.q: How did Dickie usually travel about the town, and what did he refuse to carry even when it was raining heavily?
questions.zh: 迪基平时怎样在镇上出行？即使下大雨他拒绝带什么？
questions.a: He hardly ever used his large car and preferred always to go on foot; even when it was raining heavily, he refused to carry an umbrella.
questions.aZh: 他很少使用那辆豪华轿车，总喜欢以步代车；即使大雨倾盆，他也拒绝带伞。
questions.hint: 见课文“Though he owned a large car, he hardly ever used it, preferring always to go on foot.”与“Even when it was raining heavily, he refused to carry an umbrella.”。

questions.q: What did Dickie do after the assistant refused to serve him, and how did he finally pay for the watch?
questions.zh: 店员拒绝接待之后迪基做了什么？他最后用什么方式付表钱？
questions.a: He left the shop without a word and came back carrying a large cloth bag, which he dumped on the counter. He paid no attention when asked to leave, requested to see the manager, then handed over the bag with $300 in pennies and insisted on the assistant's counting all 30,000 pennies before he left.
questions.aZh: 他一言不发地走出商店，然后提着一个大布袋回来，重重地扔在柜台上。店员让他走开他置之不理，要求见经理，随后把装着三百英镑便士的布袋递过去，并坚持要店员点清全部三万枚便士才肯离开。
questions.hint: 见课文“Dickie left the shop without a word…”至“He insisted on the assistant's counting the money before he left -- 30,000 pennies in all!”。

questions.q: Why did the exhibition of modern paintings receive so much attention in the press, and how long did it take Dickie to stage the joke?
questions.zh: 那次现代画展为何在报界引起极大关注？迪基用了多长时间来策划这场玩笑？
questions.a: Because although the pictures were supposed to be the work of famous artists, they had in fact been painted by Dickie himself; and it took him four years to stage this elaborate joke.
questions.aZh: 因为那些画虽然号称出自名家之手，实际上却是迪基自己画的；而他为策划这场精心设计的玩笑花了四年时间。
questions.hint: 见课文最后两句，注意 had in fact been painted by Dickie 这一被动结构。

questions.q: Why does the writer call Dickie a “lovable” eccentric rather than simply a strange man?
questions.zh: 作者为什么称迪基为“可爱的”怪人，而不只是说他古怪？
questions.a: Because his oddness was harmless and unselfconscious — he disregarded social conventions without being conscious of doing anything extraordinary, and he added colour to the dull routine of everyday life. His jokes were aimed at snobs, a rude assistant and self-important critics, never at ordinary people, so they won him the love and respect of others.
questions.aZh: 因为他的古怪无害且出于无心——他不顾社会习俗，却意识不到自己做了什么特殊的事，还给平淡单调的日常生活增添了色彩。他的玩笑针对的是势利小人、无礼的店员和自命不凡的评论家，从不针对普通人，因此他赢得了别人的喜爱与尊敬。
questions.hint: 结合首段“This invariably wins them the love and respect of others…”与全文对迪基行为目的的描写。

translation:
真正古怪的人从不有意引人注意。
他们不顾社会习俗，意识不到自己所作所为有什么特殊之处。
他们总能赢得别人的喜爱与尊敬，因为他们给平淡单一的日常生活增添了色彩。
理查德。
科尔森生前是我们镇上最有名望的人之一。
他是个精明能干、有钱的商人，但镇上大部分人对他生活中的这一个方面几乎一无所知。
大家都管他叫迪基。
早在他去世前很久，他的古怪行为就成了传奇故事了。
迪基痛恨势利小人。
尽管他有一辆豪华小轿车，但却很少使用，常常喜欢以步代车。
即使大雨倾盆，他也总是拒绝带伞。
一天，他遇上一场瓢泼大雨，淋得透湿。
他走进一家高级商店，要为妻子买一块价值300英镑的手表。
但店员见他浑身泥水的样子，竟不肯接待他。
迪基二话没说就走了。
一会儿，他带着一个大布口袋回到店里。
布袋很沉，他重重地把布袋扔在柜台上。
店员让迪基走开，他置之不理，并要求见经理。
经理认出了这位顾客，表示了深深的歉意，还严厉地训斥了店员。
店员为迪基拿出了那块手表，迪基把布口袋递给他，口袋里面装着300镑的便士。
他坚持要店员点清那些硬币后他才离去。
title: A Lovable Eccentric
subtitle: 可爱的怪人

lead.question: 一位精明富有的商人为何被店员拒之门外？他又是怎样不动声色地报复的？
lead.warmup: 你也许见过这样一类人：穿着随便、行为古怪，却让整条街的人都喜欢他。课文里的迪基就是这样一位“可爱的怪人”——他明明是镇上最精明富有的商人，却偏偏喜欢步行、拒不带伞、痛恨势利小人。有一天下大雨，他浑身泥水地走进一家高级商店买表，店员竟不肯接待他。他会怎样回应呢？读时请留意作者如何用让步和对比，把一个怪人写得令人敬佩。
goals: 掌握 eccentric、snob、bedraggled、collection 等核心词汇，理解 a lovable eccentric 这类名词短语的用法。
学会用 though、even when 引导的让步状语从句和 preferring… 分词短语，写出对比鲜明的句子。
熟悉 hardly ever、invariably、intensely 等频度与程度副词的位置和语气差别。
能用被动语态与非限制性定语从句复述迪基买表和画展恶作剧的经过。
lead.summary: 课文先说真正古怪的人从不有意引人注意，却总能赢得别人的喜爱与尊敬，因为他们给平淡的日常生活添了色彩。接着介绍迪基：他是精明富有的商人，却以古怪出名——很少用豪车、雨天拒不带伞、痛恨势利小人。他被大雨淋得浑身泥水进店买三百英镑的手表，遭店员拒绝，便用一布袋三万枚便士让店员当场点清。他还请评论家参观自己的“现代画收藏”，那些画其实出自他本人之手，用四年时间证明评论家并不总知道自己在说什么。
lead.tips: 频度副词的位置要记牢：hardly ever、invariably、intensely 放在实义动词之前、be 动词和助动词之后；hardly 本身含否定，不可再加 not。

exercises.q: 汉译英：真正古怪的人从不有意引人注意。
exercises.a: True eccentrics never deliberately set out to draw attention to themselves.

exercises.q: 汉译英：尽管他有一辆豪华轿车，却很少使用，总喜欢以步代车。
exercises.a: Though he owned a large car, he hardly ever used it, preferring always to go on foot.
exercises.note: though 让步，分词短语作状语

exercises.q: 句型转换（改被动语态）：Dickie had in fact painted the pictures.
exercises.a: The pictures had in fact been painted by Dickie.
exercises.note: 过去完成时被动 had been done

exercises.q: 用非限制性定语从句合并：The pictures were supposed to be the work of famous artists. They had in fact been painted by Dickie.
exercises.a: The pictures, which were supposed to be the work of famous artists, had in fact been painted by Dickie.
exercises.note: 非限制性定语从句用逗号隔开

exercises.q: 填空：Dickie was known ___ us all ___ Dickie, and his eccentricity had become legendary.
改错：He insisted on the assistant to count the money before he left.
exercises.a: He insisted on the assistant's counting the money before he left.
exercises.note: insist on + 动名词/所有格

exercises.q: 用括号中词的适当形式填空：Our neighbour is a little ___ (eccentricity), rather ___ (forget) about his own affairs, but extremely ___ (consider) to children.

quiz.q: 店员拒绝接待迪基的直接原因是什么？
options: He had no money with him.
He was in a bedraggled condition after a heavy shower.
He was wearing an old hat.
He refused to speak to the assistant.

quiz.q: 关于迪基的汽车，课文是怎么说的？
options: He sold his large car years ago.
He owned a large car but hardly ever used it.
He used his car only on rainy days.
He never owned a car of his own.

quiz.q: 迪基用什么支付那块三百英镑的手表？
options: A cheque for £300.
A cloth bag containing 30,000 pennies.
Three hundred pound notes.
The manager's credit card.
quiz.note: 三万枚便士，让店员点数

quiz.q: 经理认出这位顾客后有什么反应？
options: He called the police at once.
He laughed at the assistant.
He was most apologetic and reprimanded the assistant severely.
He refused to sell the watch.

quiz.q: 迪基的画展为何在报界引起极大关注？
options: The pictures were sold at a very low price.
The pictures were supposed to be by famous artists but had been painted by Dickie.
The critics refused to attend the exhibition.
